run: cross-owner edge pruning ablation with same-session reference arms
source_dir: work/edge-prune-m64 (ignored; binaries excluded from the archive)

ablation.edges_removed: adjacency entries whose target owner fails this query's qualification; entry lists and every qualified adjacency row are kept verbatim in original order
ablation.semantics: traversal rejects such a target before computing a distance and never marks it visited, so the pruned graph returns identical IDs with identical distance/expansion counts
ablation.enforced_checks: per query and cell: identical result IDs, identical distances and expansions, CSR-layout cross-check, identical hits, and batch checksum equality on every timed pass; any failure aborts before a CSV row is written
ablation.build_cost: per-query copy construction, measured separately and excluded from every timer
ablation.timing_protocol: fan-out batch protocol: 16 passes per batch, 10 rounds, median; the two arms alternate order every round

reference.why: archived run2 absolute times are up to 3x slower than this session for the same binary and inputs, so the QPS ratio is re-measured here instead of rescaled
reference.arms: dag_merge (merged) and nodeann (per-graph, n=k), both with 120 queries, pareto mode
reference.measured_at: immediately before the ablation runs, same machine, same taskset CPU

not_claimed: pruning as an implementable optimisation (per-query copy costs ~28-30 ms/query)
decomposition of the remaining NodeANN gap into layering, local-graph size and candidate-heap costs
